items.title: Posterior Inter-Antral Linear Ablation Using Pulsed Field Energy: Electrophysiological Validation and Early Clinical Outcomes.
items.abstract: Durable conduction block across the left atrial roof remains challenging because of complex anatomy and limitations of thermal energy delivery. Pulsed field ablation (PFA) may enable a short posterior inter-antral line as an adjunctive strategy beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI), providing linear conduction block at a more inferior posterior LA location than a conventional roofline. However, its electrophysiological characteristics and clinical relevance remain uncertain. In this single-center, nonrandomized comparative cohort study, a prospectively enrolled cohort undergoing PVI plus posterior inter-antral linear ablation was compared with contemporaneous patients undergoing PVI without additional left atrial ablation. The primary clinical endpoint was atrial arrhythmia recurrence beyond a 90-day blanking period. Propensity score matching was the primary comparative analysis; inverse probability of treatment weighting and multivariable Cox regression were sensitivity analyses. Among 306 patients, 65 underwent posterior inter-antral linear ablation and 241 underwent PVI alone. Posterior-line ablation produced characteristic reciprocal pacing responses and a caudal-to-cranial posterior wall activation pattern consistent with conduction block. During a median follow-up of 198 days, atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 4 of 65 (6.2%) versus 38 of 241 (15.8%) patients. In the primary PSM analysis, posterior inter-antral linear ablation was associated with lower recurrence (HR 0.23; 95% CI 0.07-0.78), with consistent results in sensitivity analyses. Posterior inter-antral linear ablation using PFA provides a reproducible electrophysiological pattern of conduction block and was associated with lower short-term atrial arrhythmia recurrence than PVI alone in patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. These findings warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

items.title: Heart failure beyond cardiology: a primary care perspective on the 2026 ESC guideline.
Polymer-specific nanoplastic exposure, mitochondrial dysfunction, and depressed ejection fraction in humans.
items.abstract: Micro- and nanoplastics (MNPs) are increasingly found in humans, but cardiac and energetic effects are unclear. In older adults without major comorbidities, blood levels of PS/PE were quantified, and left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) was measured by transthoracic echocardiography. To investigate polymer-specific cardiotoxic mechanisms, human AC16 cardiomyocytes were exposed to PS- or PE-nanoplastics. Mitochondrial function was assessed using Seahorse XF analysis, and molecular remodeling was characterized using transcriptomics and label-free quantitative proteomics.In humans, circulating PS and PE levels were each associated with EF in univariable analyses. PS and PE concentrations were higher in participants with EF <50% than in those with EF ≥50% (PE p=0.021; PS p<0.001). After multivariable adjustment for anthropometric and metabolic determinants of systolic function, PS remained independently associated with EF. In vitro, both polymers accumulated intracellularly and elicited mitochondrial stress. Chronic PS exposure induced a loss of respiratory capacity and bioenergetic reserve, with suppression of basal and maximal respiration and markedly reduced spare respiratory capacity. PE exposure produced a distinct remodeling pattern characterized by reduced maximal respiration, but increased ATP-linked respiration and tighter respiratory coupling, consistent with a compensatory state of reduced metabolic flexibility. Transcriptomic profiling revealed polymer-specific transcriptional phenotypes, with PE driving broader repression of cardiomyocyte structural, electrophysiological, and mitochondrial gene programs, whereas PS triggered a more restricted but coherent response. Proteomic profiling further identified a mitochondria-centered injury signature involving disruption of mitochondrial protein import and cristae organization, impairment of oxidative metabolism, altered redox buffering, and incomplete activation of mitochondrial quality-control pathways. Nanoplastic exposure is associated with left ventricular systolic function in humans and induces polymer-specific cardiomyocyte remodeling in vitro. PS is strongly linked to systolic impairment, consistent with a mitochondria-centered cardiotoxic phenotype. These findings identify nanoplastics as a previously unrecognized environmental determinant of myocardial vulnerability and support polymer-specific risk stratification.

items.title: Redefining Cardiometabolic Disease: Expert Consensus on the CardioVascular-Kidney-Liver-Metabolic (CVKLM) Multiorgan Staging.
items.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases increasingly manifest as interconnected dysfunction across the heart, vasculature, kidneys, liver, and metabolic system. The global rise in obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes, together with therapies benefiting multiple organs, has reshaped the epidemiology and understanding of cardiometabolic disease, exposing the limitations of organ-specific or single-stage approaches. The cardioVascular-kidney-liver-metabolic (CVKLM) framework is a multidimensional staging system in which cardiac, vascular, kidney, liver, and metabolic involvement are graded independently from absent to advanced. Analogous to tumour-node-metastasis staging, it provides a standardized language describing disease severity within each organ and its distribution across organs. Rather than replacing existing classifications, CVKLM integrates universal heart failure stages, validated vascular risk assessment, KDIGO chronic kidney disease stratification, contemporary metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and advanced liver disease criteria, and current definitions of diabetes and clinical obesity. Unlike hierarchical frameworks assigning a single overall stage, CVKLM preserves organ-specific information and records coexisting abnormalities across domains. Intended for clinical and research phenotyping and staging rather than as a validated global risk score, it may facilitate systematic recognition of concomitant organ disease, support existing organ-specific diagnostic, referral, and treatment pathways, and provide a standardized taxonomy for observational studies and clinical trials. The prognostic significance of CVKLM profiles, their incremental value beyond established risk tools, and their clinical utility remain to be established. By integrating these domains within a common architecture, CVKLM offers a pragmatic framework spanning the full spectrum of cardiometabolic disease, from preclinical involvement to advanced multiorgan failure.

items.title: Weekly Journal Scan: PREMIUM evidence that aspirin omission in STEMI patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention is unjustified and unsafe.
Electro-Aesthetic Regulation Enabled by Piezoelectric Signaling.
items.abstract: Aesthetic and reconstructive repair requires biomaterials that restore tissue architecture while controlling contour fidelity, scar quality, mechanical compliance, and long-term morphological stability in dynamically loaded environments. However, conventional fillers, scaffolds, and wound-care materials largely act as passive supports and offer limited capacity to adaptively regulate the regenerative microenvironment. In this Review, we present piezoelectric signaling as a mechanoelectrical strategy for electro-aesthetic regulation, whereby endogenous tissue motion or externally applied mechanical energy is converted into localized bioelectrical cues. We establish a bioelectrical information framework in which mechanical inputs are encoded into spatiotemporally organized electrical signals and biologically decoded through ion-channel activation, Ca 2 + signaling, cytoskeletal remodeling, immune regulation, angiogenesis, and extracellular matrix reorganization. We further examine how molecular polarity, crystalline phase, structural architecture, and interfacial coupling govern signaling across naturally derived biomolecules, synthetic polymers, inorganic materials, and hybrid piezoelectric systems. Representative applications include dermal repair and scar modulation, PLLA-based regenerative fillers and emerging injectable electroactive platforms, craniofacial reconstruction, multimodal stimulation, and sensing-enabled closed-loop bioelectronics. Key translational challenges include signal dosimetry, hydrated-state stability, degradation-dependent performance, biosafety, structural fidelity, and standardized aesthetic evaluation. Piezoelectric signaling may therefore shift aesthetic and reconstructive repair from passive structural restoration toward adaptive, bioelectrically mediated, and feedback-guided regulation.

items.title: Pharmacological ON/OFF Regulation of CAR T Cells through Estrogen Receptor-Based Stabilization and Targeted Degradation.
items.abstract: Regulation of therapeutic cell response is important for safe and effective therapy, particularly for immunotherapy. Ideally, the regulators should be based on human proteins using compounds that have already been approved for human use. Regulation of protein degradation by small molecules enables fast cellular response and a small genetic footprint of genetic constructs. Here, we present a clinically compatible strategy for reversible pharmacological control of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell function using human estrogen receptor (ER)-based degron domains and FDA-approved small molecules. By fusing tamoxifen-responsive ER ligand-binding domains to CARs, we generate ligand-inducible ON-switch CARs whose stability, signaling, and effector functions are precisely controlled by 4-hydroxytamoxifen. Furthermore, we demonstrate that ER-tagged CARs can be selectively degraded using the FDA-approved ER-targeting PROTAC ARV-471, establishing a complementary OFF-switch mechanism that suppresses CAR expression and effector function. Notably, these results expand the ON-OFF switch platform for post-translational control of therapeutic proteins, offering new opportunities to improve the safety and precision of cellular immunotherapies.

items.title: Spatio-temporal dynamics, transmission hotspots, and vaccination gaps driving measles persistence in Nigeria, 2006-2025.
items.abstract: Measles remains a major public health concern in Nigeria, contributing disproportionately to the global burden. Persistence of the disease is driven by sub-optimal vaccination coverage and heterogeneous transmission patterns, but the specific spatio-temporal dynamics and the quantitative impact of vaccination gaps at the sub-national level are not fully characterized. This study aimed to provide a comprehensive analysis of measles transmission in Nigeria from 2006 to 2025, with the specific objectives to identify spatial hotspots, quantify their temporal persistence, and evaluate the association between MCV1/MCV2 coverage and measles case ratio. We conducted a national retrospective ecological study, integrating 19 years of surveillance data (2006-2025) and geospatial information, with a focused 4-year analysis of vaccination records (2021-2024). Analytical methods included time-series decomposition, spatial autocorrelation (Local Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi*), and linear mixed-effects modeling to quantify vaccination effects while accounting for state-level heterogeneity. Analysis of 253,595 measles cases revealed a highly clustered geographic distribution, with 86.4% of the national burden concentrated in northern Nigeria. We identified 38 persistent hotspot Local Government Areas that accounted for 23.2% of all cases. Vaccination coverage was low and disparate, with national averages of 73.8% for MCV1 and 38.4% for MCV2. Mixed-effects modeling confirmed a significant negative association between MCV1 coverage and the measles case ratio, while MCV2 coverage did not show a statistically significant independent effect. Measles transmission in Nigeria is driven by entrenched hotspots in the north and critical vaccination gaps threatening disease resurgence in the south. Achieving elimination requires a tailored strategy: intensive supplemental immunization activities and RI strengthening aimed at reducing endemic transmission in the northern hotspots, coupled with focused efforts to close routine immunization gaps in specific southern states.

items.title: Single-cell multi-omics reveals archetypal regulatory programs shared across T cell subsets.
items.abstract: T cells differentiate into functionally distinct subsets in response to pathogens, yet essential immune functions such as self-renewal, expansion, cytokine production, and cytotoxicity are common to multiple subsets and therefore must be programmed via shared regulatory mechanisms. To uncover these "archetypal" epigenomic programs, we integrated a single-cell multiomic (scATAC+RNA-seq) dataset of CD4 and CD8 T cells responding to acute and chronic viral infection with a comprehensive bulk ATAC-seq compendium. Our analysis reveals a modular architecture governing T cell identity, implicating distinct transcription factors in reusing regulatory programs across subsets and lineages. Notably, translationally important progenitor CD8 T cells, critical for sustained immunity and present in both acute and chronic infection, exhibit a composite regulatory state, combining a CD8 exhaustion program with a follicular helper CD4 T cell program. In sum, this resource and generalizable computational framework will aid the mechanistic dissection of adaptive immunity and immunotherapy design.

items.title: Adverse events of herpes zoster vaccination among adults in Saudi Arabia: A cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: The varicella-zoster virus, which causes herpes zoster upon reactivation, remains a public health concern, particularly among older adults. Although Zostavax and Shingrix are effective vaccines, monitoring adverse events remains important. Limited vaccine uptake and low public awareness in Saudi Arabia further highlight this need. This study seeks to assess the adverse events linked to herpes zoster immunization throughout the Saudi Arabian population. This cross-sectional study used a Google Form questionnaire administered from 16 September 2024-15 August 2025. A total of 382 participants completed the survey. The largest age subgroup was 18-25 years (22.3%). For the first dose, 185 participants (48.4%) did not know the vaccine type, whereas 144 (37.7%) received Zostavax and 53 (13.9%) received Shingrix. Among second-dose recipients (n = 152), 85 participants (55.9%) received Zostavax, 41 (27.0%) received Shingrix, and 26 (17.1%) were uncertain of the vaccine type. The most frequently reported adverse effects after the first dose were fatigue/headache, injection-site pain, and dizziness, whereas chills, injection-site pain, and dizziness were most frequent after the second dose. No adverse effects were reported by 112 participants (29.3%) after the first dose and 28 (18.4%) after the second dose. Participants who received Zostavax reported significantly higher self-reported severity scores than those who received Shingrix after both the first dose (p = 0.003) and the second dose (p < 0.001). Self-reported symptom severity was higher among participants with chronic disease and varied significantly by age after the first dose. The most commonly reported symptom duration was 1-2 days. No significant gender differences were observed. In unadjusted analyses, participants who reported receiving Zostavax had higher self-reported severity scores than those reporting Shingrix.

items.title: Despite High Hepatitis C Virus Testing, Treatment Gaps Remain: A Study Among Syringe Services Program Participants in Massachusetts.
items.abstract: People who inject drugs are less likely to initiate hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, and less likely to achieve sustained virologic response if they do start, than the general population. The objective of this analysis was to examine whether healthcare experiences were associated with HCV testing and treatment outcomes among people who inject drugs in Massachusetts. We analyzed baseline data from an HIV prevention study, which enrolled participants from two Massachusetts syringe service programs from 2020 to 2025. We assessed lifetime HCV testing and treatment outcomes, sociodemographics, substance use behaviors, and healthcare experiences (e.g., comfort with providers) and calculated bivariate associations. Among 185 participants (median age of 40, 43% cisgender women), 97% had ever been tested for HCV; 71% of those tested had ever received a positive test result. However, among those who tested positive, only 41% initiated treatment. Most participants reported comfort discussing their injection drug use with a provider (79%) and feeling welcome in medical clinics (75%). Cisgender men and those feeling welcome in medical clinics reported higher proportions of treatment initiation compared to their counterparts (both p<0.05). Despite pervasive testing and high treatment completion rates, treatment initiation remains suboptimal. Feeling welcome in medical clinics may be an important, modifiable indicator of HCV treatment engagement. The gap between HCV testing and treatment initiation persists. Understanding factors that shape HCV testing and treatment engagement can generate actionable insights for ongoing elimination efforts in New England.

items.title: Hepatitis C viral variants bear signatures of de novo CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure after spontaneous postpartum viral suppression.
items.abstract: Progression to chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection entails loss of HCV-specific CD4+ T cell help, emergence of viral variants that escape recognition by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies, and exhaustion of CD8+ T cells targeting remaining intact epitopes. Once chronic infection has been established, it is generally lifelong without treatment. However, in some chronically infected women, a surprising postpartum viral load decline has been linked to resurgent functional HCV-specific CD4+ helper T cells. A minority of women even spontaneously clear long-standing chronic infection postpartum. To test whether restored T cell help boosts HCV-specific CD8+ T cell or antibody responses in women with postpartum viral control, we performed serial near-full-length deep sequencing of HCV genomes to assess evolution of viral MHC class I epitopes and antibody epitopes in nine women with significant postpartum viral declines (≥ 1 log 10 at 3 mo postpartum, "controllers") and 12 with more stable levels ("noncontrollers"). Although not associated with mutations arising early postpartum, at 12 to 24 mo postpartum, viral control was strongly associated with amino acid mutations in epitopes predicted to be targeted by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies. Plasma from controllers also demonstrated a postpartum increase in neutralization of multiple HCV strains. Together, these findings support the hypothesis that postpartum viral control is mediated by CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure.
items.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

items.title: Multi-Virus Surveillance Across Diverse Freshwater Systems in Tehran, Iran.
items.abstract: Environmental surveillance of viral contaminants in water systems is an essential tool for assessing exposure risk and supporting early-warning frameworks for emerging infectious diseases. In this study, a comprehensive one-year surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 and six enteric viruses was conducted across diverse freshwater systems in Tehran, Iran - including rivers, wells, and traditional qanat (underground aqueduct) infrastructures. Water quality parameters (turbidity, pH, Total Dissolved Solids, nitrate) and fecal bacterial indicators (total coliforms, fecal coliforms, and E. coli) were also measured to contextualize viral contamination within a broader environmental risk framework. Between September 2020 and August 2021, a total of 118 water samples were collected and analyzed using quantitative molecular detection methods. Overall, 61 of 118 samples (51.7%) tested positive for at least one virus. Surface water (rivers) showed substantially higher contamination rates (80.3%; 53/66 samples) compared to groundwater (15.4%; 8/52 samples). Among groundwater sources, qanat systems were markedly more vulnerable than conventional wells, with 25.0% (6/24) of qanat samples testing positive versus only 7.1% (2/28) of well samples. This elevated contamination in qanats was dominated by rotavirus (5/6 positive qanat samples, detection rate 20.8%) and was associated with higher fecal bacterial loads (total coliform geometric mean: 245 MPN/100 mL in qanats vs. 28 MPN/100 mL in wells), consistent with the susceptibility of shallow horizontal collection channels to fecal infiltration. SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected in 34.8% of river samples and 3.9% of groundwater samples, with concentrations reaching 1.28 × 10⁴ genome copies per liter (GC/L) in surface waters, demonstrating sustained fecal contamination across all seasons. The most prevalent viruses in river water were norovirus GII (45.5%), adenovirus (43.9%), rotavirus (42.4%), and norovirus GI (40.9%), with mean concentrations ranging from 1.26 × 10² to 3.76 × 10³ GC/L. Hepatitis A and E viruses were not detected in any sample. Seasonal variation in viral detection was observed for enteric viruses, while SARS-CoV-2 and adenovirus showed year-round persistence. Strong correlations between fecal indicators and viral contamination (Spearman r = 0.61-0.63) support the use of bacterial monitoring as a cost-effective screening proxy. The results highlight the particular vulnerability of qanat systems and underscore the value of integrated environmental surveillance for water safety management in arid, water-stressed urban environments.

items.title: A quick guide to select pediatric vaccine-preventable diseases.
items.abstract: Resurgent outbreaks and declining childhood vaccination coverage have amplified the need for pediatricians to promptly recognize and manage vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs). This review summarizes the epidemiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, initial management, public health reporting, and prevention of selected VPDs relevant to pediatric practice. Childhood vaccination coverage has declined in recent years, coinciding with renewed outbreaks and continued transmission of measles, mumps, pertussis, meningococcal disease, and hepatitis B in the United States. Recent federal immunization schedule changes for children and adolescents (e.g., revised hepatitis B birth-dose guidance, altered meningococcal vaccine decision-making, and expanded pentavalent meningococcal vaccine options) highlight the need for pediatricians to remain familiar with evolving vaccine recommendations. Although routine immunization has dramatically reduced the burden of many VPDs, recent declines in vaccine coverage and notable outbreaks have renewed the need for clinical vigilance. Pediatricians should be prepared to identify characteristic presentations, implement appropriate isolation and infection-control measures, obtain timely diagnostic testing, initiate treatment or postexposure management when indicated, and reinforce vaccination as the cornerstone of prevention. This review provides a practical guide to the recognition and management of measles, mumps, pertussis, meningococcal disease, and hepatitis B in pediatric settings.

items.title: Transcriptome Analysis of Hepatitis C Virus-Infected Hepatoma Cells Following Stringent Removal of Genomic DNA.
items.abstract: Hepatitis C Virus (HCV) is a positive strand RNA virus that infects hepatocytes and reprograms cellular gene expression, contributing to chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma. HCV replicates slowly and induces limited changes in the cellular transcriptome. Here, we improved analysis of low-abundance transcripts, including long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), in the context of HCV replication. We stringently removed genomic DNA from total RNA from Huh-7 hepatoma cell lines by a combination of TRIzol, acidic phenol, silica matrix columns and recombinant DNase I. RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) and targeted validation were used to characterize Lnc-ITM2C-1 splice variants and expression of its neighboring gene, G protein-coupled receptor 55 ( GPR55 ), to investigate their potential roles in HCV replication. Challenging our previous findings, under our improved experimental conditions, Lnc-ITM2C-1 and GPR55 were neither involved in a positive regulation circuit with HCV nor induced detectable transcriptome changes. Secondary analysis of RNA-Seq data according to HCV infection status revealed statistically robust HCV-induced expression of 21 host cell genes involved in pathways like stress response (in particular ATF3), lipid metabolism, cytoskeleton organization and growth regulation. In contrast, we found that expression changed for only a limited subset of previously reported HCV-associated lncRNAs (e.g., EGOT). This highlights the necessity of stringent gDNA removal for analysis of low-abundance transcripts like lncRNAs.

items.title: Mechanistic insights into ENO2-driven glycolysis and tumor progression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
items.abstract: Neuron-specific enolase 2 (ENO2) has been implicated in tumor metabolism, but its biological role in hepatocellular carcinoma remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to investigate the expression, prognostic relevance, and functional role of ENO2 in HCC. Public transcriptomic datasets, RNA sequencing, WGCNA, survival analyses, and pathway enrichment analyses were integrated to identify HCC-associated genes. ENO2 expression was validated in HCC cell lines and paired clinical tissues.Gain- and loss-of-function, catalytic-rescue, glycolytic-inhibition, and pyruvate-rescue experiments were performed to evaluate glycolytic activity, proliferation, colony formation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth. ENO2 was upregulated in HCC and was associated with advanced tumor stage and unfavorable survival outcomes in public datasets. ENO2 overexpression increased glycolytic activity and malignant phenotypes, whereas ENO2 depletion produced opposite effects. In ENO2-depleted cells, re-expression of shRNA-resistant ENO2 wild type restored the impaired glycolytic and malignant phenotypes, whereas the catalytic-deficient ENO2 mutant failed to restore them. Moreover, 2-deoxy-D-glucose attenuated ENO2 overexpression-associated phenotypes, while pyruvate partially rescued phenotypes associated with ENO2 depletion. ENO2 expression was also associated with altered PI3K and AKT phosphorylation. ENO2 may contribute to HCC progression by enhancing glycolytic metabolism and malignant phenotypes, partly in association with PI3K/AKT signaling. ENO2 is a candidate metabolic and prognostic biomarker that requires validation in larger independent clinical cohorts and warrants further investigation as a therapeutic candidate.

items.title: Radioembolization for Colorectal Liver Metastases: Indications and Outcomes.
items.abstract: Colorectal cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with the liver representing the predominant site of metastatic spread. For patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) who are not candidates for surgical resection, systemic chemotherapy provides disease control but rarely achieves durable hepatic responses. Radioembolization with yttrium-90 (Y-90) microspheres, delivered via the hepatic artery to exploit the preferential arterial supply of liver tumors, has emerged as an important locoregional option in this setting. This review examines the current evidence base for radioembolization in CRLM, covering patient selection, indications across lines of therapy, dosimetric advances, and clinical outcomes. Appropriate candidacy requires careful assessment of performance status, hepatic tumor burden, tumor biology, lung shunt fraction, and extrahepatic disease extent, with the strongest outcomes observed in patients selected earlier in their disease course. Randomized controlled trials support second-line and third-line use, while unselected first-line use has not demonstrated a benefit. Dosimetric advances, including multicompartment personalized dosing, radiation segmentectomy, and radiation lobectomy, are enabling ablative and bridge-to-resection strategies in appropriately selected patients. Future investigation should prioritize biomarker-driven patient selection, personalized dosimetry, and combination strategies with systemic therapy to determine whether durable hepatic disease control can translate into a survival benefit.

items.title: The role of tyrosine kinase inhibitors as a post-hematopoietic stem cell transplant continuation therapy for pediatric acute leukemia: a systematic review.
items.abstract: Relapse following hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) is a leading cause of transplant failure for pediatric acute leukemia patients, emphasizing the need for an effective post-transplant continuation therapy. This systematic review evaluates the role of tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) as a post-HSCT continuation therapy in pediatric acute leukemia. A literature search of PubMed, Cochrane, Web of Science, and VHL was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Original studies were included if they were relevant to the research question and fit the eligibility criteria. The initial search identified 765 articles, with 16 studies included after filtration. TKIs were indicated for patients with chromosomal alterations causing constitutively active kinase signaling. Common agents included imatinib, dasatinib, ponatinib, sorafenib, and gilteritinib, and selection was based on disease status and molecular profiling. Duration of continuation ranged from 10 months to 3 years, with dosage dependent on the agent and tolerability. TKIs were generally well-tolerated, with reported side effects including cytopenia, liver dysfunction, and skin conditions. Across the included studies, MRD negativity and sustained molecular remission were reported in selected patients receiving post-HSCT TKI continuation therapy, while relapse was also reported after treatment discontinuation or in resistant disease. However, optimal duration and long-term safety remain unclear in the pediatric population. TKIs can serve as a targeted post-HSCT continuation therapy in select pediatric acute leukemia patients, particularly those with high-risk, mutation-driven disease. Molecular profiling and MRD monitoring are central to guiding agent selection, timing, and mutation-directed therapy adjustments. These findings support individualized TKI treatment to reduce relapse risk following HSCT, while highlighting the need for prospective studies to define standardized treatment strategies.

items.title: Novel algorithm for the diagnosis and treatment of different types of bile leakage following liver surgery.
items.abstract: Posthepatectomy bile leakage (PHBL) after liver resection with bilioenteric anastomosis may originate from the anastomosis (anastomotic leak (AL)) or the transection surface (surface leak), including leakage from isolated bile ducts (IBDLs). Differentiating these sources remains challenging, and standardized management guidelines are lacking. All patients undergoing liver resection with bilioenteric anastomosis from 2008-2023 were analysed. PHBL was classified by origin (AL, surface leak, IBDL) and timing (early versus late onset). Drain fluid bilirubin concentration, drain-to-serum bilirubin ratio, and daily bilirubin loss were evaluated by leak type. Outcomes of conservative, interventional, and surgical management were compared. Among 2936 liver resections, 229 involved bilioenteric anastomosis. PHBL occurred in 96 patients, including 44 ALs (46%), 47 surface leaks (49%), and 5 IBDLs (5%). AL showed higher peak drain bilirubin than surface leak/IBDL (38.3 versus 18.6 mg/dl; P 20.85 mg/dl, drain-to-serum ratio > 10.57, and bilirubin loss > 160.93 mg/day. Management success varied by type and timing: AL and IBDL responded best to reoperation (success rates 78% and 100%), whereas surface leak was more effectively managed without surgery (65%). In AL specifically, reoperation was more successful in early-onset leaks (65% versus 38% in late-onset; P = 0.069), whereas interventional therapy was more successful in late-onset leaks (58% versus 15% in early-onset; P = 0.003). Distinct diagnostic thresholds help differentiate AL from other PHBL types. AL and IBDL benefit from reoperation, whereas surface leak is better managed without surgery. Timing influences therapeutic success, supporting a novel type- and timing-based management algorithm for PHBL.
